title: Enzymes with One Job: Dibucaine Number, Serum ACE and Acid Phosphatase
summary: Phenotype pseudocholinesterase with the dibucaine number, interpret serum ACE as supportive (not diagnostic) evidence for sarcoidosis, and see why PSA replaced prostatic acid phosphatase for early prostate cancer detection.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 21 Hit 12 (dibucaine number), Hit 15 (serum ACE in sarcoidosis) and Trap 6 (prostatic ACP vs PSA). Checked against Panhuizen 2010, Jońca 2015, Delacour 2014, Zencirci 2009, Crouser 2020 (ATS), Zheng 2023, Kraaijvanger 2020, Kong 2013, Muniyan 2013 and Xu 2019. The reviewer’s fixed DN bands (70–90 / 50–70 / 10–30) are method-dependent: Jońca 2015 shows DN depends on substrate and dibucaine concentration (register flag rv-dibucaine-method-ranges). The reviewer says variant carriers are the ones with prolonged apnoea; Zencirci 2009 reports heterozygotes show at most about 50% prolongation while homozygotes can stay paralysed for hours (rv-dibucaine-carrier-apnea). Hit 15’s “classic picture” adds elevated ACE to Löfgren’s syndrome, which the ATS guideline defines without ACE; ACE inhibitors and ACE I/D genotype also distort ACE (rv-sarcoid-ace-confounders). Trap 6’s “nearly all extracapsular/metastatic cases elevate it” was not found (rv-acp-metastatic-elevation). Pending: Number Vault ACP, ACE and PChE figures, mivacurium-specific claims, Löfgren triad wording. The IFCC LD method PDF (Bais 1994) was behind a captcha and was not used.

objectives: Interpret cholinesterase activity and the dibucaine number to identify usual, heterozygous and homozygous atypical phenotypes.
Explain why serum ACE supports but does not diagnose sarcoidosis, and name factors that distort it.
State why prostate-specific antigen replaced prostatic acid phosphatase for early prostate cancer detection.

scenes.title: Three enzymes, three questions
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three requests reach the chemistry bench — (1) a patient who stayed paralysed for hours after succinylcholine, with low cholinesterase activity and a dibucaine number of 20; (2) a patient with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and a high serum ACE, labelled “ACE high, so sarcoidosis confirmed?”; (3) a request for acid phosphatase to screen a healthy man for early prostate cancer. Question token: “What does each enzyme really tell you?”

cues.text: Three requests reach the chemistry bench. A patient stayed paralysed for hours after succinylcholine; the dibucaine number is twenty.
A patient with enlarged hilar lymph nodes has a high serum ACE, and someone wants acid phosphatase to screen a healthy man for early prostate cancer.
What does each enzyme really tell you, and what can it not tell you?

props.label: What does each enzyme really tell you?

scenes.title: Where each enzyme comes from
scenes.altText: Schematic: three source cards. Butyrylcholinesterase (pseudocholinesterase, BChE) is made in the liver and released into plasma, where it hydrolyses succinylcholine and mivacurium. Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) is expressed by the epithelioid and giant cells of granulomas, so granuloma burden raises serum ACE. Prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP) is a prostate enzyme: low in healthy serum, elevated in metastatic prostate cancer and correlating with stage.

cues.text: Butyrylcholinesterase, also called pseudocholinesterase, is made in the liver and released into plasma. It breaks down the muscle relaxants succinylcholine and mivacurium.
Angiotensin-converting enzyme is expressed by the epithelioid and giant cells that build granulomas. More granuloma means more ACE in serum.
Prostatic acid phosphatase comes from the prostate. It is low in healthy people, rises in metastatic prostate cancer, and tracks with stage.

scenes.title: The dibucaine number
scenes.altText: Dibucaine card: the dibucaine number (DN) is the percentage of BChE activity inhibited by dibucaine. The usual enzyme is strongly inhibited (DN about 70 or higher); the atypical variant resists dibucaine (DN 30 or less); heterozygotes fall in between (DN 58 in one carrier of an atypical-plus-Kalow allele; 60–80 under one lab’s conditions). Cut-offs depend on substrate and dibucaine concentration. Risk card: low activity with DN under 30 suggests a high risk of prolonged paralysis; homozygous atypical patients can stay paralysed for hours; heterozygotes show only modest prolongation (up to about 50%). Activity and DN answer different questions: how much enzyme versus which kind.

cues.text: The dibucaine number is the percentage of cholinesterase activity that dibucaine inhibits. The usual enzyme is strongly inhibited, giving a number of about seventy or more.
The atypical variant resists dibucaine, so homozygotes give thirty or less. Heterozygotes fall in between. Exact cut-offs depend on the substrate and dibucaine concentration used.

Low activity with a dibucaine number under thirty suggests high risk. Homozygous atypical patients can stay paralysed for hours after succinylcholine; heterozygotes usually have only a modestly longer block.
So measure both. Activity says how much enzyme there is; the dibucaine number says which kind it is.

props.label: Activity = how much · DN = which kind

scenes.title: ACE and acid phosphatase in context
scenes.altText: ACE card: about 30–80% of sarcoidosis patients have raised serum ACE; sensitivity 22–86%, specificity 54–95%. Also raised in tuberculosis, berylliosis, histoplasmosis, Gaucher disease and other conditions. ACE inhibitors make serum ACE uninterpretable; the ACE insertion/deletion genotype shifts levels (DD highest, II lowest). Serum ACE can help monitor treatment. The ATS 2020 guideline lists elevated ACE among supporting features; diagnosis usually rests on a compatible presentation, nonnecrotising granulomas and exclusion of other causes. PAP card: PSA has largely replaced PAP for early detection because PSA is more sensitive; PAP remains a prognostic marker in advanced and metastatic disease.

cues.text: Serum ACE is raised in roughly thirty to eighty percent of sarcoidosis patients, and it also rises in tuberculosis, berylliosis, histoplasmosis and Gaucher disease. It supports the diagnosis; it does not make it.
ACE inhibitor drugs make the result uninterpretable, and the ACE gene insertion or deletion genotype shifts the normal level. Serial ACE can help monitor treatment.
The diagnosis usually rests on a compatible picture, nonnecrotising granulomas on biopsy, and exclusion of other causes.
Prostate-specific antigen has largely replaced acid phosphatase for early detection, because it is more sensitive. Acid phosphatase still carries prognostic weight in advanced and metastatic disease.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A dibucaine number of 20 is a heterozygous carrier” (✓ 30 or less with low activity is homozygous atypical: high risk of hours-long paralysis); “High serum ACE confirms sarcoidosis” (✓ supportive only; raised in other granulomatous diseases, affected by ACE inhibitors and genotype); “Order acid phosphatase to screen for early prostate cancer” (✓ PSA is more sensitive and replaced it; PAP is prognostic in advanced disease).

cues.text: Trap one: a dibucaine number of twenty is a heterozygous carrier. No: thirty or less is the homozygous atypical pattern, the high-risk one.
Trap two: a high serum ACE confirms sarcoidosis. No: it supports the diagnosis, and tuberculosis and other granulomatous diseases raise it too.
Trap three: order acid phosphatase to screen for early prostate cancer. No: prostate-specific antigen is more sensitive and replaced it.

scenes.title: Lock, witness, veteran
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “Dibucaine is a LOCK test — the usual enzyme gets locked (high DN), the atypical one slips free (low DN). ACE is a WITNESS — it supports the case but cannot convict. PAP is a VETERAN — retired from early screening, still consulted on advanced disease.” Tokens: lock = dibucaine · witness = ACE · veteran = PAP. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: dibucaine is a lock test. The usual enzyme gets locked, so the number is high; the atypical enzyme slips free, so it is low. ACE is a witness: it supports, it cannot convict. Acid phosphatase is a veteran, retired from early screening.

Where it breaks: dibucaine cut-offs vary with the method; a silent-allele carrier can have lower activity with a near-usual dibucaine number; and serum ACE is also distorted by ACE inhibitors and genotype.

explanation.what: Plain language: some enzymes are ordered for one specific question. Pseudocholinesterase clears a muscle relaxant, and a drug test (dibucaine) shows whether the enzyme is the normal kind. Granuloma cells make ACE, so a high level hints at sarcoidosis. Acid phosphatase comes from the prostate but was replaced by PSA for finding early cancer. Scientific terms: butyrylcholinesterase (BChE, pseudocholinesterase), dibucaine number (DN), atypical (dibucaine-resistant) variant, silent variant, succinylcholine, mivacurium, angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), epithelioid and giant cells, nonnecrotising granuloma, ACE insertion/deletion (I/D) polymorphism, prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP), prostate-specific antigen (PSA).
explanation.why: BChE hydrolyses succinylcholine and mivacurium, so low or atypical enzyme prolongs paralysis. Granuloma epithelioid and giant cells express ACE, raising serum levels in proportion to granuloma burden. Serum PAP rises in metastatic prostate cancer, but PSA detects early disease more sensitively.
explanation.measure: DN = percent of BChE activity inhibited by dibucaine: usual about 70 or higher, atypical homozygotes 30 or less, heterozygotes in between; low activity with DN under 30 suggests high risk. Cut-offs depend on substrate and dibucaine concentration. Serum ACE: raised in about 30–80% of sarcoidosis, sensitivity 22–86%, specificity 54–95%; ATS lists it as a supporting feature. PAP: low in health, elevated in metastatic disease and correlating with stage.
explanation.differs: Activity (how much enzyme) vs DN (which kind); homozygous atypical (hours of paralysis) vs heterozygote (modest prolongation); supportive marker (ACE) vs diagnosis (picture + nonnecrotising granuloma + exclusion); early detection (PSA) vs prognosis in advanced disease (PAP).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: assign a phenotype from a dibucaine number, pick the drug to avoid, choose the best statement about serum ACE, or explain why acid phosphatase is not used for screening.

questions.stem: A patient remains paralysed for hours after succinylcholine. Plasma cholinesterase activity is low and the dibucaine number is 20. What is the most likely phenotype?

options.rationale: Correct. Low activity with a dibucaine number of 30 or less is the high-risk homozygous atypical pattern (a compound atypical/silent genotype can look similar).
Incorrect. The usual enzyme is strongly inhibited by dibucaine, giving about 70 or more.
Incorrect. Heterozygotes give intermediate values and usually only a modestly longer block.
Incorrect. In one reported family a silent/usual carrier had lower activity but a near-usual dibucaine number of about 75.

questions.stem: Which statement about serum angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) in suspected sarcoidosis is correct?

options.text: It supports the diagnosis but can also be raised in tuberculosis and other granulomatous diseases
options.rationale: Correct. ACE is supportive; tuberculosis, berylliosis and histoplasmosis can raise it too.

options.text: An elevated level confirms sarcoidosis without biopsy
options.rationale: Incorrect. ACE is only supportive; diagnosis usually needs a compatible picture, nonnecrotising granulomas and exclusion of other causes.

options.text: It is raised in nearly every patient with sarcoidosis
options.rationale: Incorrect. Only about 30–80% of patients have a raised level.

options.text: It is unaffected by ACE inhibitor therapy
options.rationale: Incorrect. ACE inhibitors make serum ACE uninterpretable for diagnosis or monitoring.

questions.stem: A clinician asks for prostatic acid phosphatase to screen a healthy man for early prostate cancer. What is the best response?

options.text: PSA has largely replaced it for early detection because PSA is more sensitive
options.rationale: Correct. PAP is not sensitive for early-stage disease; PSA displaced it.

options.text: Acid phosphatase is the preferred screening test
options.rationale: Incorrect. It was displaced by PSA for detection.

options.text: Acid phosphatase has no clinical value at all
options.rationale: Incorrect. It remains a prognostic marker in advanced and metastatic disease.

options.text: Acid phosphatase is low in metastatic prostate cancer
options.rationale: Incorrect. Serum PAP is elevated in metastatic disease and correlates with stage.

Homozygous atypical: paralysis for hours; heterozygotes up to about 50% prolongation.

Granuloma epithelioid/giant cells express ACE; 30–80% raised, sensitivity 22–86%, specificity 54–95%; raised in TB, berylliosis, histoplasmosis, Gaucher; ACE inhibitors and I/D genotype distort; helps monitoring.

claims.note: Not taught as stated. DN cut-offs vary by method (Jońca 2015); the ATS guideline defines Löfgren’s syndrome without ACE; no source read gives the ACP “nearly all” figure.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 21 Hit 12 gives fixed DN bands (usual 70–90%, heterozygotes 50–70%, homozygous variants 10–30%). Jońca 2015 shows DN depends on dibucaine concentration and substrate (UU >80 and UA 60–80 under their conditions), and Delacour 2014 reports a silent/usual carrier with a near-usual DN of 75.3; bands should be read as method-dependent (register flag rv-dibucaine-method-ranges).

Ch. 21 Hit 12 says “the variant carriers are the ones who get prolonged apnea”. Zencirci 2009 reports heterozygotes show up to about 50% prolongation of block, whereas homozygous atypical patients can be paralysed for hours (Panhuizen 2010), and Delacour 2014 notes prolonged block occurs with marked deficiency (impairment over 70%); the major risk sits with homozygotes and compound genotypes, although Zencirci also notes that one or more atypical alleles can prolong mivacurium paralysis (register flag rv-dibucaine-carrier-apnea).

Ch. 21 Hit 15 gives the classic picture as bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy + erythema nodosum + elevated ACE. The ATS 2020 guideline defines Löfgren’s syndrome as bilateral hilar adenopathy with erythema nodosum and/or periarticular arthritis, without ACE; reviews add that ACE inhibitors make serum ACE uninterpretable and the ACE I/D genotype shifts levels (register flag rv-sarcoid-ace-confounders).

Ch. 21 Trap 6 says nearly all extracapsular/metastatic cases elevate ACP. Sources read state PAP is elevated in metastatic disease, correlates with stage and is prognostic, but give no “nearly all” figure (register flag rv-acp-metastatic-elevation).

morphology.note: No micrographs; enzymes shown as cards.
